current_episode.title: You're Not Burned Out - You're Bored Out: Mitch Matthews on Reigniting Your Fire

guest.bio_context: Mitch Matthews started his career in pharmaceutical sales before being promoted into a bad-fit role that pushed him to explore coaching and speaking on the side. He built a full-time coaching and speaking business that surpassed his previous income within five months. Over the past 25 years, he has coached executives, entrepreneurs, leaders, and thousands of coaches and speakers, and created a program called the Authority Bridge to help high-capacity professionals add coaching or speaking without disrupting their existing careers.

5 months: time it took Mitch Matthews to surpass his pharmaceutical salary with his coaching and speaking business after launching full-time
15 minutes: the daily novelty injection recommended by neuroscientist Anne-Laure Le Cunff as sufficient to combat 'bored out' in high achievers
$20,000: example paid speaking fee cited by Mitch Matthews as the level at which audiences and event organizers treat speakers with significantly greater intentionality and engagement
9-figure valuation: host Mick's AI company valuation achieved approximately one and a half years after founding, attributed in part to Mitch Matthews' 'dream bigger' coaching framework
$50 million: the initial valuation target Mick set for his AI company before applying Mitch Matthews' 'dream bigger' mindset, which led to a nine-figure result

pending_qa.q: What is Mitch Matthews' Authority Bridge program and who is it designed for?
pending_qa.r: The Authority Bridge is a program Mitch Matthews created for executives, entrepreneurs, founders, and leaders who want to add coaching or speaking to their professional life — typically as a side avenue — without starting from scratch or blowing up their existing career. It grew from Mitch's observation that his most successful clients were leaders who became coaches and speakers on the side, which reignited their passion, brought additional income, and renewed their sense of impact.

pending_qa.q: How does getting paid for speaking change the impact and experience for Authority Bridge clients?
pending_qa.r: Mitch Matthews uses the example of a VP of Sales in his Authority Bridge program who had been doing speaking for free but was losing his fire. Mitch coached him on how to get paid for speaking, noting that when someone is paid $20,000 for a talk, the audience is more intentional, the introduction is better prepared, and attendees are more engaged. According to Mitch, this creates a win-win: more impact for the speaker and more income.

pending_qa.q: What role did Mitch Matthews' wife play in his career pivot from pharmaceuticals to coaching?
pending_qa.r: When Mitch was struggling in his bad-fit pharmaceutical role, his wife noticed his fire was going out and took action. She placed a magazine in front of him with a sidebar about an entrepreneur's coach and told him directly, 'That's what you do — that's what you've done since the day I've known you.' She was the catalyst who identified coaching as his path before he even knew it existed as a profession.

pending_qa.q: What phrase did Mitch Matthews receive in a moment of self-doubt among high achievers, and what does it mean?
pending_qa.r: While in a green room surrounded by his heroes and feeling intense impostor syndrome, Mitch Matthews says he prayed and received a simple phrase: 'Learn from, don't compare to.' He uses this as a guiding principle for high achievers to draw inspiration from others without falling into destructive self-comparison.

pending_qa.q: What early career clues pointed Mitch Matthews toward his future in coaching?
pending_qa.r: Mitch traces his coaching instincts back to childhood, when helping a friend would pull him out of anxiety spirals. Later, working at a bike shop in Iowa, he excelled not by knowing the most about bikes but by asking customers what kind of riding they wanted to do — a discovery-through-curiosity approach. The same pattern repeated in pharmaceutical sales, where he built deep personal connections with doctors, nurses, and receptionists by genuinely caring about their lives and dreams.
